text: yep ok now did u also catch that it creates two faces on opposite ends as the same face? thats the same bug im showing you now, is look at the piece i have selected. how is that even possible? 1 create face is 2 parts on opposite ends, where selecting one of the faces selects both. it thinks its one piece
resolution: The 'two faces on opposite ends selecting as one piece' bug: adoptAppendedFaces stamped ONE fresh group id across every triangle appended in a transaction, so mirror-bilateral extrude-edge/create-face fused the twin and its source into a single authored face (inspect proved tris at x=-0.5 and x=+0.5 sharing group 123). Fixed: the appended range partitions into per-face segments (source, then each twin), each minting its own group id (nextFreeGroupId is max+1 so consecutive ids are free), and Create Face's focus handoff now selects only the SOURCE face — bilateral ops still pair twins positionally. Headless proof on the rebuilt binary: mirrored edge extrudes produce distinct groups (+x quad and -x twin), every authored group is one contiguous quad, no group owns disjoint opposite-side islands.
